newsitem.title: UK: Britain planning second evacuation from Tirana.
newsitem.headline: Britain planning second evacuation from Tirana.

text.p: Britain escorted 131 British and other nationals from the Albanian capital Tirana to the port of Durres on Thursday and said it would repeat the operation on Friday for its remaining stranded citizens.
A Foreign Office spokesman said any Britons still in Tirana should gather outside the British embassy at 7 a.m. local time (0500 GMT) on Friday.
The 131 taken to Durres were still waiting late on Thursday for a boat to take them to Italy, he said by telephone.
Albania slid towards anarchy on Thursday as arms depots in several towns were looted and people used the weapons to raid food warehouses for emergency stockpiles.
The Foreign Office spokesman said earlier on Thursday that Tirana airport was no longer under government control and groups of armed civilians were moving freely around the city.
"There are frequent bursts of gunfire in the centre of the city. There is a risk of widespread public disorder and looting tonight," he said.

The United States has already ordered 160 government employees and their families to leave Albania, where armed rebels are demanding the resignation of President Sali Berisha. It has urged another 2,000 Americans to go.
